__structural_preservation_prefix__:
CRITICAL STRUCTURAL PRESERVATION — READ BEFORE ALL ELSE:
This is a before/after interior redesign, NOT a new photo. The output image must be the EXACT SAME PHOTOGRAPH as the input, with only the furniture, decor, and colours changed digitally — like a virtual staging overlay on top of the original photo.
You must preserve with PIXEL-LEVEL fidelity:
- The exact camera position, angle, height, tilt, and field of view — do not regenerate the shot, do not reframe, do not zoom in or out, do not shift left or right
- The exact room geometry: floor area, ceiling height, wall angles, room proportions
- The walls exactly as they appear in the original photo — same colour, same paint finish, same texture, same material, same condition, same trim and skirting boards. The walls are NEVER repainted, recoloured, retextured, or replaced, even if the chosen style would normally suggest a different wall colour
- Every architectural element in its exact original position: windows (size, position, wall), doors (position, which wall), archways, columns, beams, niches, fireplaces, built-in structural features
- Floor material texture and colour family unless the style prompt explicitly overrides it
- Natural light direction, shadows, and ambient light temperature exactly as in the original photo
IDENTIFYING WALLS VS FURNITURE:
- Before changing anything, correctly distinguish between actual walls (the room's fixed vertical surfaces, ceiling-to-floor, behind everything else) and furniture or objects that happen to sit close to or against a wall (such as wardrobes, bookshelves, sofas, headboards, cabinets, or large items pushed flush against a wall)
- Large furniture pieces positioned near or against a wall must NOT be mistaken for part of the wall — these are movable objects and ARE part of the redesign, even if they span a large area or touch the wall surface
- Only the true underlying wall surface (visible behind, above, or around furniture) is locked and preserved — the furniture itself in front of that wall is freely replaced as part of the new design
ABSOLUTE RULES:
- Do NOT generate a new camera angle, perspective, or viewpoint under any circumstances
- Do NOT alter room layout, floor plan, proportions, ceiling height, or any structural detail
- Do NOT change the wall colour, wall paint, wall texture, or wall material under any circumstances, regardless of what the style prompt below describes
- Do NOT move, resize, remove, or reposition windows or doors
- Do NOT add fixed installations that do not exist in the original photo: no new ceiling lamps or pendant lights, no wall-mounted shelves, no crown moulding or stucco, no new radiators, fireplaces, or built-in units — freestanding, movable furniture and lamps are the only additions allowed
- Do NOT crop, zoom, pan, tilt, or reframe the image in any way
- If in doubt, treat the original photo as a locked background plate and only swap out movable objects within it
OUTPUT QUALITY: Photorealistic, 4K architectural visualisation, natural daylight, clean render.
ONLY the furniture, soft furnishings, decorative objects, and movable lighting are replaced. The camera, structure, light, and walls stay IDENTICAL to the input photo, no exceptions.
scandinavian/living_room/tier1:
ROOM FUNCTION: living room. Create a comfortable seating zone with a properly upholstered sofa or compact equivalent, a usable coffee or side table and appropriate storage. Add an armchair only if circulation permits. If a TV is present or requested, retain a plausible screen and seating sightline without blocking windows or making the TV the decorative focal point. Keep rugs and curtains scaled to the actual room; leave natural floor breathing space.

STYLE: Skandinavisk (scandinavian). Create an unmistakably Scandinavian interior: light natural oak, ash or birch; warm off-white, oatmeal, pale sand and gentle warm grey; airy proportions, functional simplicity and tactile natural-looking textiles. Use slender legs or visually light bases, calm rounded edges and a balance of useful furniture and breathing space. Upholstered seating has fabric-covered cushions and an optional visible light-wood frame or legs, not a solid wooden seat block. Small muted sage, dusty blue or charcoal accents are optional. Keep this light wood and textile identity across every tier. Avoid dominant dark walnut, heavy stone blocks, extensive gold, glossy hotel styling and a compulsory all-beige palette.

TIER: tier1. Budget specification: use well-proportioned standard-size pieces and simple construction, honest laminate or veneer, painted surfaces, everyday woven upholstery and practical ceramic or porcelain where relevant. Prefer straightforward edges, modest hardware and a small amount of coordinated decor. Make the room thoughtfully finished and welcoming without implying expensive bespoke fabrication. Use the selected style's budget material options; do not age, damage or cheapen the photograph.

VISIBLE STYLE-SPECIFIC SPECIFICATION: Use simple birch or pale-oak-look veneer, warm white painted storage, linen-look cotton upholstery, a flatwoven rug and plain ceramic details. Keep shapes light and practical.

ROOM-SPECIFIC TIER DETAIL: Choose a straightforward upholstered sofa, compact practical table and simple movable storage; finish with a small coordinated textile accent.

STYLE APPLIED TO THIS ROOM: Use oatmeal or warm-grey fabric seating with a light-oak frame or legs, a softly rounded light-wood table and an airy woven textile accent.

__canonical_integrity__: Edit the supplied original property photograph into a believable photograph of the same space. Keep the original camera position, height, lens perspective, field of view, framing, orientation and aspect ratio. Preserve room dimensions, ceiling height, wall and ceiling planes, openings, window frames, doors, beams, columns, radiators, existing architectural mouldings and fireplace geometry. Preserve the outdoor view and weather. Do not create extra floor area, another room, a window, doorway, skylight, arch, structural niche or fireplace. Retain the original daylight direction, time of day and daylight intensity wherever daylight is present. For windowless or artificially lit input, retain that lighting situation; do not invent daylight or windows. Let changed materials and objects produce physically plausible local shadows, reflections and light bounce. Any permitted supplemental lighting must remain restrained and consistent with the source exposure; do not turn day into dusk or wash the room in orange light. Respect the selected edit scope. Style and tier never expand what may be changed. The selected room function determines the necessary furnishings, subject to the visible space and fixed service zones. Apply style references to sofas, upholstery, rugs, curtains or decorative lamps only where that function and location support them. In utility, wet or exercise zones translate the palette into appropriate existing functional elements; do not add living-room furniture merely because a shared style or tier paragraph mentions it. Scale and select furnishings from the available evidence; do not infer exact measurements or hidden floor area. Keep believable walking routes, door swings, cabinet access and radiator/window access clear. Use fewer or smaller suitable pieces when space is limited. Furniture examples describe a design direction, not a requirement to fit every item. Preserve explicitly requested existing items within the allowed scope; otherwise replace dated movable furnishings with a coherent new set appropriate to the selected style. Choose materials appropriate to use: moisture-suitable finishes in wet rooms, practical work surfaces, impact-appropriate exercise surfaces and weather-suitable outdoor materials. Use tier to change visible material specification and detailing, never photo quality, room size or furniture quantity by default. Use a supplied style reference only for material, colour and form; never copy its geometry, openings or view. If no style reference is supplied, use the written style definition and do not invent an unseen reference. Render natural material variation, precise joins, believable edges, fabric texture, contact shadows and coherent reflections. Keep window frames and visible exterior detail naturally resolved within the source exposure; do not invent a sharper or different view. No synthetic blur, plastic sheen, repeated texture stamps, warped fixtures, floating objects, exaggerated HDR, excessive sharpening, text, borders, logos, watermarks or interface elements. Aim for clean, comfortable, plausibly inhabited interiors photographed professionally, with restrained relevant everyday details. Return one finished image at the requested supported output size. Resolution is an output setting, not a tier effect.
__canonical_furnishing_scope__: EDIT SCOPE: FURNISHING ONLY. Replace or rearrange movable furniture, rugs, textiles, freestanding storage, art and decor, and freestanding lamps. Preserve wall and floor finishes, ceiling fixtures, mounted installations, kitchen cabinetry and appliances, bathroom fixtures, plumbing, fitted joinery and all other fixed fittings. Do not add or remove fixed installations. Express the chosen style through the permitted movable elements. Apply any fixed-finish, cabinet, fixture or integrated-lighting suggestions in the preset only as a material or colour reference for allowed movable pieces; they do not authorize renovation in this mode. When few movable changes are possible, produce a modest credible restyling, not an invented renovation.
__canonical_renovation_scope__: EDIT SCOPE: SURFACE AND FITTING RENOVATION VISUALIZATION. In addition to movable furnishings, renew visible wall paint or nonstructural surface finish, floor finish on the same plane, cabinetry, countertops, backsplash and room-appropriate fixtures within the original layout and service zones. Keep the structural shell and architectural features specified above intact; do not hide, remove or reshape openings, beams, radiators, structural niches or fireplace geometry to obtain the style. In kitchens keep the current cabinet footprint, appliance locations, sink zone and cooking zone. Renew their appearance and fitted units within those zones. Retain existing island or peninsula geometry; do not add an island where none exists. In bathrooms keep toilet, basin, bath and shower functions in their existing zones. Renew their visible fixtures, enclosure and wall/floor finishes without adding new wet zones. Do not add a tub, second basin, separate shower or extra appliance unless the original layout already accommodates that function or the user's explicit instruction and clear visual evidence support it. In other rooms fitted storage may follow an existing clear wall only when circulation remains plausible; do not cut niches into walls or manufacture extra depth. Replace a light fixture at an existing plausible mounting point; under-cabinet or furniture-integrated light may accompany authorized renewed cabinetry. Do not invent new ceiling recesses or a grid of spotlights. Where installation space is uncertain, use a suitable freestanding lamp. This is a visual concept, not proof of construction feasibility.
__canonical_conflicts__: CONFLICT RESOLUTION: Camera, shell geometry, existing light situation, allowed edit scope and physical fit take priority. Within those limits follow the user's explicit room function and retain/change wishes, then room requirements, then the selected style and tier. A style example never authorizes forbidden construction or overrides access. If the full furnishing list cannot fit, retain essential function using fewer or smaller pieces. For renovation, the selected scope expressly authorizes only the surface and fitting changes listed in that scope; do not append an incompatible blanket ban on repainting, cabinetry or fixture renewal. For furnishing-only, style descriptions do not grant any renovation permission.
